stages.name: Roman-held
stages.desc: Rome, its colonies and loyal allies

stages.name: Gallic & Alpine
stages.desc: Gauls, Ligurians and Alpine peoples outside Roman rule

stages.name: Contested
stages.desc: Armies in the field; towns split between the two sides

stages.name: With Hannibal
stages.desc: Most communities have gone over to Hannibal or Carthage

stages.name: Recovered by Rome
stages.desc: Taken back by Rome after a defection or revolt

states.name: Valle d'Aosta
timeline: Alpine valleys of the Salassi, a Celtic people outside Roman rule

states.name: Piemonte
timeline: Taurini and other Ligurian and Gallic peoples of the upper Po
Hannibal comes down from the Alps and storms the chief town of the Taurini

states.name: Lombardia
timeline: Rome's war on the Insubres: Marcellus wins at Clastidium and Mediolanum falls
The Insubres submit to Rome after the fall of Mediolanum
The colony of Cremona is founded; Hannibal arrives and wins the cavalry fight on the Ticinus
The Insubres throw off Roman rule; only the colony of Cremona holds out

states.name: Trentino-Alto Adige
timeline: Raetic and other Alpine peoples, outside Roman rule

states.name: Liguria
timeline: Ligurian hill peoples, often at war with Rome
Ligurians send men to Hannibal's army

states.name: Emilia-Romagna
timeline: The Boii have submitted to Rome since 224 BC; Ariminum is a Roman colony
The Boii rise and join Hannibal; he destroys a Roman army at the Trebia
The Boii wipe out Postumius's army in the Litana forest; Placentia and Ariminum hold

states.name: Marche
timeline: Picenum and the ager Gallicus, settled by Roman colonists
After Trasimene, Hannibal plunders Picenum on his way to the Adriatic
Picenum stays loyal

states.name: Veneto
timeline: The Veneti and the Gallic Cenomani, allies of Rome against the Insubres

states.name: Friuli-Venezia Giulia
timeline: The Carni and other peoples of the eastern Alps

states.name: Abruzzo
timeline: Marsi, Paeligni, Vestini and Marrucini, loyal allies of Rome

states.name: Molise
timeline: The Pentri Samnites, allies of Rome
Hannibal winters at Gerunium; Fabius rescues his rash deputy Minucius
The Pentri stay loyal while other Samnites go over to Hannibal

states.name: Apulia
timeline: Daunian towns, the Latin colony of Luceria and Greek Tarentum, all allied to Rome
After Cannae, Arpi, Salapia, Herdonea and others go over to Hannibal
Fabius's son retakes Arpi
Hannibal takes the city of Tarentum; the Roman garrison holds the citadel
Salapia returns to Rome; Hannibal destroys a Roman army at Herdonea
Fabius retakes Tarentum; after Canusium, Hannibal withdraws south

states.name: Basilicata
timeline: Lucanian hill towns and the Latin colony of Venusia
Most Lucanians go over to Hannibal; Venusia holds for Rome
The Greek cities of Metapontum and Heraclea join Hannibal
Marcellus fights Hannibal to a draw at Numistro
Some Lucanian communities surrender to Rome
Marcellus is killed in an ambush near Venusia

states.name: Calabria
timeline: Bruttian hill peoples and Greek cities: Rhegium, Locri, Croton
The Bruttians go over to Hannibal
Locri and Croton fall to the Bruttians and Carthaginians; Rhegium holds for Rome
Bruttium remains Hannibal's last stronghold in Italy

states.name: Campania
timeline: Capua, Nola, Neapolis and the rich Campanian plain
Hannibal ravages the Falernian plain and slips past Fabius
Capua and the Hirpini go over to Hannibal; Marcellus holds Nola
Fabius and Marcellus retake Casilinum
Capua surrenders to Rome after a two-year siege

states.name: Lazio
timeline: Rome and the Latin cities
Hannibal marches on Rome and camps by the Anio, then withdraws
Twelve Latin colonies refuse to send more soldiers

states.name: Toscana
timeline: Etruscan cities, allies of Rome
Hannibal crosses the marshes of the Arno and ravages Etruria
Etruria stays loyal after Hannibal marches south
Unrest at Arretium; Rome takes hostages from the Etruscan nobility

states.name: Sicily
timeline: Roman province in the west; Hiero II's Syracuse, Rome's ally, in the east
Hiero dies; his grandson Hieronymus turns toward Carthage
Syracuse goes over to Carthage; Marcellus storms Leontini
Marcellus besieges Syracuse; a Carthaginian army takes Agrigentum
Syracuse falls to Marcellus
Laevinus takes Agrigentum and all Sicily is Roman again

states.name: Sardegna
timeline: Roman province since 238 BC
Hampsicora's revolt and a Carthaginian landing, crushed by Manlius Torquatus
Sardinia is secured for Rome

states.name: Umbria
timeline: Umbrian towns and Roman colonies such as Spoletium
Flaminius's army is destroyed at Lake Trasimene; Spoletium beats off Hannibal
Umbria stays loyal

events.title: Clastidium
events.text: Marcellus kills the Insubrian king Viridomarus in single combat and routs his cavalry.

events.title: Mediolanum falls
events.text: Marcellus and Scipio Calvus take the chief town of the Insubres, who submit to Rome.

events.title: The spolia opima
events.text: Marcellus dedicates the king's armour to Jupiter Feretrius, the third and last Roman to do so.

events.title: Via Flaminia
events.text: The censor Gaius Flaminius builds the great road from Rome to Ariminum.

events.title: New colonies
events.text: Rome founds Placentia and Cremona on the Po to hold down the Gauls.

events.title: Over the Alps
events.text: Hannibal comes down into Italy with some twenty-six thousand men and a few elephants.

events.title: Taurini stormed
events.text: Hannibal storms the chief town of the Taurini, who refused his alliance.

events.title: Ticinus
events.text: Hannibal's cavalry beats the consul Scipio, who is saved by his young son.

events.title: Trebia
events.text: Hannibal lures a Roman army across the icy river and destroys it.

events.title: Lake Trasimene
events.text: A Roman army is ambushed in the fog beside the lake; the consul Flaminius is killed.

events.title: Fabius the Delayer
events.text: Quintus Fabius Maximus is named dictator and refuses to give battle.

events.title: Falernian plain
events.text: Hannibal ravages Campania and escapes Fabius by driving oxen with burning torches.

events.title: Gerunium
events.text: Hannibal winters at Gerunium; Fabius rescues his rash deputy Minucius.

events.title: Cannae
events.text: Hannibal encircles eight Roman legions and their allies; perhaps fifty thousand die.

events.title: Capua defects
events.text: The second city of Italy opens its gates to Hannibal.

events.title: Marcellus at Nola
events.text: Marcellus holds Nola and drives off Hannibal's attack, Livy's first Roman success after Cannae.

events.title: Litana forest
events.text: The Boii ambush and destroy the army of Postumius.

events.title: Casilinum starved
events.text: The small garrison of Casilinum surrenders to Hannibal after a winter siege.

events.title: Second battle of Nola
events.text: Livy records a second victory for Marcellus outside Nola; historians suspect he exaggerates.

events.title: Locri and Croton
events.text: The Greek cities of the toe of Italy fall to Hannibal's Bruttian allies.

events.title: Sardinian revolt
events.text: Hampsicora rises with Carthaginian help; Manlius Torquatus crushes the revolt.

events.title: Hiero dies
events.text: Rome's ally Hiero II of Syracuse dies after more than fifty years in power.

events.title: Casilinum retaken
events.text: The consuls Fabius and Marcellus recapture Casilinum.

events.title: Beneventum
events.text: Gracchus's army of slave volunteers defeats Hanno and wins its freedom.

events.title: Leontini
events.text: Marcellus storms Leontini; reports of a massacre drive Syracuse into Carthage's camp.

events.title: Archimedes' machines
events.text: Catapults and cranes devised by Archimedes defeat Marcellus's assault on Syracuse.

events.title: Arpi retaken
events.text: Fabius's son recovers Arpi, the first great Apulian city back in Roman hands.

events.title: Agrigentum
events.text: A Carthaginian army lands in Sicily and takes Agrigentum.

events.title: Tarentum
events.text: Hannibal takes Tarentum by night; the Roman garrison holds out in the citadel.

events.title: Syracuse falls
events.text: Marcellus takes the city during a festival of Artemis; Archimedes is killed.

events.title: Herdonea
events.text: Hannibal destroys the army of the praetor Fulvius Flaccus.

events.title: Hannibal at the gates
events.text: Hannibal marches on Rome to break the siege of Capua, then turns away.

events.title: Capua surrenders
events.text: Capua falls; its leaders are executed or take their own lives.

events.title: The ovation
events.text: Marcellus enters Rome in an ovation with the art of Syracuse.

events.title: Salapia
events.text: Salapia's leaders betray Hannibal's Numidian garrison to Marcellus.

events.title: Second Herdonea
events.text: Hannibal destroys the army of Fulvius Centumalus and razes the town.

events.title: Numistro
events.text: Marcellus and Hannibal fight all day in Lucania without a clear result.

events.title: Sicily secured
events.text: Laevinus takes Agrigentum and ends the war in Sicily.

events.title: Canusium
events.text: Marcellus loses the first day; Livy claims he won the second at heavy cost.

events.title: Tarentum retaken
events.text: Fabius, consul for the fifth time, takes back Tarentum.

events.title: Twelve colonies refuse
events.text: Exhausted Latin colonies such as Ardea refuse to send more soldiers.

events.title: Ambush near Venusia
events.text: Marcellus is killed scouting a hill between the camps; his colleague Crispinus is mortally wounded.

events.title: The signet ring
events.text: Hannibal sends forged letters sealed with Marcellus's ring; Salapia sees through the trick.

events.title: Arretium
events.text: Rome takes hostages from Etruscan nobles at Arretium, fearing a revolt.

chartNote: Share of the area of modern Italy, by the allegiance of each present-day region. Regions are today's boundaries, not the peoples of the time, and the map is a simplification: in most regions some towns held for Rome while others went over to Hannibal. Dates follow Livy and Polybius and are approximate.
